incident: KwaZulu-Natal floods (eThekwini and surrounds), April 2022. Baseline for comparison.

basics.deaths: 435-459 (443 widely reported; Amnesty 2025: 'around 435 people died and another 80 were reported missing')
basics.affected: 19,113 households, 128,743 people (IFRC final report, cited by Amnesty 2025)
basics.displaced: Displaced families moved to 120 mass care centres, then 14 Transitional Emergency Accommodation sites; 1,049 families still in TEAs in June 2025
basics.damage_usd: About ZAR 17 billion (about USD 963 million), provincial government estimate (Presidential Climate Commission, cited by Amnesty 2025)
basics.rainfall: Record-breaking. World Weather Attribution: probability 'approximately doubled due to human-induced climate change'; intensity up 4-8%

I01_governing_party_and_help.finding: KZN was ANC-governed in April 2022, and the President visited (Clermont and other sites) with the Premier. After an IFP-led coalition took over the province in June 2024, no presidential visit was found for the deadly Feb and Mar 2025 KZN floods. All 9 presidential flood visits 2016-2026 were to ANC-governed provinces.

I02_election_effect.finding: Ward 9 (Molweni, a named flood and missing-persons area) changed from DA to ANC in an Oct 2023 by-election, a result attributed to unfixed flood-damaged bridges and roads. There is no systematic study of flood effects on the 2024 vote. The full test is the 4 Nov 2026 local election, for which there is a 2021 ward turnout baseline.
I02_election_effect.url: data/raw/original_lastmile-data (eThekwini ward baseline, citing Daily Maverick)

I03_election_timing_and_visits.finding: Presidential visit on 13 Apr 2022, not close to an election (the next national election was May 2024). The 2019 Easter-flood visit came about 2 weeks before the May 2019 election.

I04_declaration_threshold_and_funds.finding: National state of disaster declared on 18 Apr 2022. The Auditor-General found the relief response 'too slow': water was not provided quickly enough, owing to lack of preparedness, capacity and project management.

I05_infrastructure_repair_and_accountabi.finding: AGSA: 20% of 30 temporary residential units inspected 'were built on unsuitable land as they were close to the riverbank'. In Feb 2025, 5 people died in the Lamontville temporary relocation area that eThekwini built on the Umlazi riverbank. Molweni bridges remained unfixed into 2023.

I06_health_facility_disruption.finding: Floods 'washed away homes, schools, health centres and critical infrastructure' (Amnesty). No facility count was found in our sources.

I08_waterborne_disease.finding: Water supply was cut for days and people used poor-quality water (AGSA). No outbreak figures were found in our sources.

I09_displacement_shelter_and_mental_heal.finding: 120 mass care centres; the SAHRC called conditions 'worrying and potentially dangerous'. Families were then moved to 14 TEAs, with 1,049 families still there in June 2025 (3+ years). Residents report fear, overcrowding and violence.

I10_child_deaths_and_timing.finding: Children were among the dead, e.g. the Sokhela family in Clermont lost four children after a church wall collapsed. Residents describe the water arriving at night ('It was 2 in the night, and the water came in'). No count of child deaths was found.

I12_recovery_speed_nightlights_or_rebuil.finding: Durban lost an estimated 1.8% of annual GDP, and businesses took about three months to return to pre-flood operations (Presidential Climate Commission). Permanent rehousing was still incomplete in 2025.

I13_income_employment_loss.finding: Qualitative evidence only: residents in TEAs lost jobs (e.g. domestic workers) because of relocation. No survey figures were found.

I14_relief_grants_uptake.finding: The Social Relief of Distress grant was used in major floods, but it requires a municipal 'major incident' declaration. Uptake figures were not found.

I16_observation_radar_forecast_quality.finding: SAWS issued Yellow Level 2 and then Orange Level 8 (Daily Maverick; other sources say Level 5 to 8 to 9). SAWS said its warnings were 'issued in a timely manner' but the rain 'exceeded even the' expectations. SAWS main-radar availability was 52% in FY2022/23.

I17_community_warning_systems.finding: The Quarry Road informal settlement (eThekwini/UKZN pilot since 2016: WhatsApp groups, whistles, ropes, evacuation map, ~30 minutes of warning) evacuated with no drownings; one person died by electrocution.

I18_power_telecom_outage_during_warning.finding: Floods damaged 'communication and electrical systems' (Presidential Climate Commission). No timing data on outages relative to warnings was found.

I19_warning_language_and_accessibility.finding: Official warnings were in English. The mayor said the city issued alerts, but residents said none reached them. Of about 67 April-2022 deaths we could place, 49 were at sites where 1-3% of residents speak English as a first language (Census 2011).
I19_warning_language_and_accessibility.value: English; 49 of 67 placed deaths at 1-3% English sites

I20_warning_system_design_change_after.finding: An Emergency Housing Command Centre working with SAWS was created (Apr 2023). There is still no public cell broadcast. The Early Warnings for All roadmap (2025-2029) was launched in Oct 2025. The Presidential Climate Commission recommended strengthening early warning; the Quarry Road model has not been scaled beyond 2-3 pilots.

who_died: 'Most of the deaths were in the peri-urban areas on the periphery of the city, not in informal settlements' (Daily Maverick, 7 Jun 2022). Named death sites: Inanda (14), KwaNdengezi (10), Mzinyathi (10), Clermont (4), Lindelani (3). Causes include collapsing homes and walls, being swept away, and mudslides.
blame_framing: Premier: 'avoid building their homes near river banks on areas unsafe for human settlements'. Climate framing by Daily Maverick (IPCC) and by the Premier. The mayor said alerts were issued, and residents said none reached them (accountability ambiguity).
inquiries_and_consequences: Auditor-General special reports on flood relief funds (2022); Presidential Climate Commission analysis (2023, follow-up 2025). No inquiry into the warning chain or warning language was found. Amnesty calls for an inquiry into the Lamontville relocation.
notes: Baseline assembled from this project's existing data files. Not re-researched.
